question: Does any untested combination of early, middle, late, and terminal layer bands close the source-driven compiled graph without admitting all components?
selection_rule: Combine these arms with the nine frozen v1 arms to complete all 16 band subsets. Select the jointly feasible non-all arm with the fewest allowed sites, breaking ties by lexicographic arm name. Feasibility thresholds are unchanged from v1 and must all hold under both cross-fits.

predictions.pred_a_authority_self_clamp_finiteness_a: v1 and helper authorities replay, self-clamp is exact, values are finite, and <=59 forwards execute
predictions.pred_b_complete_lattice_contains_a_prune: at least one of all 15 non-all band subsets is jointly feasible
predictions.pred_c_selected_arm_is_crossfit_stable: selected arm minimum-coordinate projections differ by <=0.05 and per-task behavioral projections differ by <=0.05 across fits
predictions.pred_d_late_and_terminal_are_jointly_nee: every jointly feasible non-all arm includes both late and terminal bands
predictions.pred_e_complete_lattice_is_monotone_at_c: the all-band arm weakly dominates every immediate three-band predecessor on minimum coordinate and behavioral projection

decision: A feasible non-all arm defines the coarse dependency support for component-level greedy deletion. If none exists, all four bands are necessary at coarse resolution and component-level deletion starts from the all-component ceiling.
